text:
jia: Quick sync — proposing a small operator refactor for regional drain/handshake during failover. TL;DR: add an explicit DrainHandshake RPC + two-phase prewarm + a short backpressure window. Thoughts?

alex: +1 to explicit RPC. we've been relying on implicit signals and it's messy. main q: how do we avoid double-evict races with the KV cache?

sam: main risk is eviction thrash when two regions think they're primary. suggested guard: a short randomized backoff on evict + a lease grace window.

jia: exactly. proposal sketch: operator sends DrainHandshake(region_from, region_to, epoch, prewarm_hint). target region replies with ACCEPT/DEFER + prewarm_token. only after ACCEPT we start cutover.

leo: I'll prototype the operator side. simple pseudo:
```
rpc DrainHandshake(req) -> { status, prewarm_token }
if status == ACCEPT -> start traffic-drain(timeout=drain_ms)
else -> backoff(random(200, 2000)ms)
```

maria: metrics we should add: handshake_attempts, handshake_accept_latency, prewarm_success_rate, eviction_conflicts. also add an alert if handshake attempts > 3x normal.

ajex: @alex (typo) meant to ping you — how does this interact with our routing SLOs? if drain_ms is too long we blow latency targets for some tenants.

alex: right. want tunables: prewarm_timeout and staged_cut fraction. small tenants can be cut instantly; big tenants need gradual ramp. maybe route-level policy: "fast-cut" vs "graceful-cut".

sam: also think about consent/residency. if tenant is EU-resident and target region is non-EU, handshake should be rejected upfront by policy check. we need a synchronous policy validation in operator.

jia: good call. add policy_check step before ACCEPT. operator will call policy-service(policy_key, region_to). if DENY -> REJECT.

maria: on the prewarm side, prewarm_token should encode expected cache keys or a hint (top 5 prefixes) so target region can prime KV cache and GPU model warmups. keep token small.

leo: question: prewarm sequencing - do we block inbound requests until prewarm completes? or allow degraded reads?

alex: allow degraded reads via replica fallback for a short window. we should not block the control plane. just mark incoming requests with header X-Drain-Mode: draining to help telemetry.

sam: fallback story: when primary is draining, route to standby using `prefer-local=false` for latency sensitive tenants. that keeps service available. add a circuit-breaker to avoid thundering herd.

jia: ops-bot: can you create a temp checklist for the playbook items below?

ops-bot: created checklist #8943: drain-handshake-rfc -> prototype, policy-check, prewarm-token-schema, metrics, unit tests, integration sim, runbook. ETA 3d. :white_check_mark: 

maria: integration sim: we need a chaos test that flips primary mid-prewarm and verifies no double-evict and no split-brain for 1k tenants. simulate network partitions.

leo: note for prototype: keep operator state machine minimal: INIT -> POLICY_CHECK -> PREWARM -> ACCEPTED -> DRAIN -> CUTOVER -> CLEANUP. all transitions event-sourced for observability.

alex: one more: rollback. if prewarm success rate < threshold, do an automatic fallback and requeue cutover for later. avoid manual ops when possible.

jia: agree. threshold configurable per-tenant tier. default 95% prewarm success or auto-abort.

sam: tiny nit: make prewarm_idempotent. retries should not re-trigger expensive full-model loads, more like resume.

maria: doc reqs: small RFC appendix on telemetry naming and a playbook section mapping alerts -> runbook steps. I'll draft.

leo: i'll open a draft PR with operator state machine + tests. will link here when ready.

jia: thanks all — plan: prototype (leo) + sim (maria) + policy integration (sam). we'll regroup in 4 days. if anyone wants to object to the handshake approach speak now. otherwise i'll convert to short RFC.

alex: sounds good. :thumbsup: 

leo: PR up: https://git.redwood/infra/ops/merge_requests/23 (WIP)

maria: adding playbook note: during cutover, ensure billing tags stay consistent to avoid charge duplication. putting that in the checklist.

ops-bot: scheduled follow-up meeting: 2025-06-02 15:00 UTC (calendar invite sent).

jia: ok closing thread — will publish RFC draft Monday.
